boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Marmiton River (Charlot's Farm, Shiloh Creek) record (October 25, 1864) in Price's Missouri Expedition [September-October 1864]. Mine Creek (KS003) and the Little Osage action the same afternoon are not added here; the destruction of the train and the retreat to Carthage are context. Campaign-wide marches, recruiting, destruction, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Two brigades, provisional cavalry division and Army of Missouri; the live field reads zero. NPS says McNeil commanded two brigades and that the Confederate line included a sizable number of unarmed men. Britton says McNeil's Second and Benteen's Fourth Brigades met Price's whole army drawn up in quadruple line, with Shelby's division in front, and that Cole brought ten guns into action. Price says he formed the unarmed men, several thousand, in line of battle on the prairie.
claims.rationale: Unit identifications and an unquantified count of unarmed men; no return. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

Britton places it on Shiloh Creek about six miles northeast of Fort Scott, after which the Confederates retreated to the Marmiton crossing ten miles east of Fort Scott; Price says the train had gone ten miles ahead to the Marmiton.
claims.rationale: Location described differently by a summary, a history and an interested report; no map verification.

open_questions: McNeil's (No. 27), Benteen's (No. 10) and Pleasonton's reports, Shelby's report and a map placing Charlot's farm and Shiloh Creek remain deferred.

Rosecrans's, Pleasonton's and Curtis's reports, the subordinate Union and Confederate reports in Volume XLI Part 1, the organization of Price's army (No. 89), Maclean's itinerary (No. 90), the Price Court of Inquiry, Hinton's 1865 Rebel Invasion of Missouri and Kansas, maps and returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family (the NPS battle page plus the frozen Arnold rows). Wiley Britton's The Civil War on the Border, volume II (Putnam, 1899) is a retrospective history by a Union participant; by its preface the larger operations are based mainly on the published official reports, so it is not independent of the Price report family. Price's September 19 and November 2 dispatches and his December 28, 1864 report (Official Records Series I, Volume XLI, Part 1, No. 88) are one family of interested Confederate accounts. The Official Records volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
